questions.question: During a walk-around inspection, make sure the release arm is properly seated and the safety latch or lock is:
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check the fifth wheel. The release arm must be properly seated and the safety latch or lock must be engaged. All parts should be present and working properly.

questions.question: Fully-loaded rigs:

options.text: Are less likely to roll over than empty rigs.
Are more likely to roll over than empty rigs.
Are just as likely to roll over as empty rigs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are more likely to roll over than empty rigs.
questions.explanation: Fully-loaded rigs roll over more easily than empty rigs. The weight of the cargo raises the center of gravity, making rollover more likely.

questions.question: Rough acceleration:

options.text: Is common if a vehicle is warmed up.
Is encouraged to improve gas mileage.

questions.explanation: Speed up smoothly and gradually so the vehicle does not jerk. Rough acceleration can harm the engine and other parts.

questions.question: Texting while driving should:
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous and illegal. You must never text while operating a commercial motor vehicle.

questions.question: Watching the road ahead:

options.text: Is more dangerous than only watching your mirrors.
Does not help you drive more safely.
Can help you avoid the need for sudden lane changes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help you avoid the need for sudden lane changes.
questions.explanation: Sudden lane changes are dangerous in combination vehicles. Look ahead for obstacles so you can plan lane changes in advance instead of making sudden moves.

questions.question: A CMV should:

options.text: Not have a fire extinguisher, unless it is being used to transport hazardous materials.
Not have a fire extinguisher, unless it will be traveling through remote areas.
Have a fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three reflective warning triangles or flares, and at least one fire extinguisher that is charged and ready to use.

questions.question: Trailers built before ____ are not required to have spring brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers built before 1975 do not need spring brakes. If parking a trailer without spring brakes, use wheel chocks to stop it from rolling.

questions.question: On a leaf spring:
questions.explanation: When inspecting suspension, check that leaf springs do not have broken or missing leaves. If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing, the vehicle must be taken out of service until it is fixed.

questions.question: Routine vehicle inspections should be done to ensure:
questions.explanation: The main reason to inspect your vehicle is safety. Regular inspections protect you and other drivers on the road.

questions.question: In low temperatures, bridges usually freeze:

options.text: After other parts of the roadway.
Before other parts of the roadway.
At the same time as other parts of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before other parts of the roadway.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before regular road surfaces in cold weather. Be extra careful on bridges and overpasses during wet, cold conditions.

questions.question: Drivers stuck behind a slow vehicle often:
questions.explanation: Many drivers tailgate slow vehicles. If someone is tailgating you, let them pass.

questions.question: Why do large vehicles use air brakes?

options.text: Other brakes are hard to find.

questions.explanation: When maintained properly, air brakes are safe and effective for stopping large, heavy vehicles.

questions.question: If you push the tractor air supply control and the trailer spring brakes do not release, you should:

options.text: Turn on the Anti-Lock Braking System.
Turn the engine off and back on.

questions.explanation: Before driving, make sure all equipment works properly. If the trailer spring brakes do not release, check that the air line connections are tight and sealed.

questions.question: If your trailer suddenly jackknifes, you should never:
questions.explanation: If the trailer jackknifes, release the brakes and let the trailer wheels grip the road. Do not use the trailer hand brake. Braking is what locked the wheels in the first place.

questions.question: What is a retarder?

options.text: A device that keeps a vehicle from going too fast.
A device that keeps a vehicle quiet.

questions.correctAnswerText: A device that keeps a vehicle from going too fast.
questions.explanation: Retarders slow vehicles down and reduce the need to use brakes.

questions.question: What kind of brakes do most newer heavy-duty trucks use?
questions.explanation: Most newer heavy-duty trucks use dual air brake systems. This means two separate air brake systems with one set of brake controls.

questions.question: A driver should use the trailer hand valve to:
questions.explanation: Using the trailer hand valve while driving can cause a skid. Use it only to test the trailer brakes.

questions.question: Do not base your gear shift decision on:

options.text: What the vehicle next to you is doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: What the vehicle next to you is doing.
questions.explanation: Shift based on your engine rpm or road speed. Learn your vehicle's rpm range and shift up at the top of that range. You can also learn which speeds work for each gear.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: It is safe to drive with one or two missing lug nuts.
A cracked lock ring is safe if you drive under 55 mph.
A missing clamp on a rim is dangerous and must be fixed.

questions.correctAnswerText: A missing clamp on a rim is dangerous and must be fixed.
questions.explanation: Missing clamps, spacers, studs, or lugs are dangerous. Mismatched, bent, or cracked lock rings are also dangerous. Check your tires and rims before driving.

questions.question: When driving a new vehicle, learn the controls:
questions.explanation: Learn all features and equipment of a new vehicle before you drive it.
